text_blocks.snippet: Treatment and prevention represent fundamentally different approaches to healthcare. Prevention focuses on avoiding illness or injury in the first place, while treatment addresses existing health issues. In essence, prevention aims to keep people healthy, while treatment aims to restore health after it has been compromised.
snippet_highlighted_words: Prevention focuses on avoiding illness or injury in the first place, while treatment addresses existing health issues

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: Preventive healthcare includes actions taken to avoid the onset of disease or injury, or to detect them early. This can involve lifestyle changes, vaccinations, screenings, and other proactive measures.
Regular checkups and screenings (like mammograms or colonoscopies) to detect potential problems early.
Promoting healthy habits like exercise, a balanced diet, and not smoking.

list.title: Goals:
list.snippet: To maintain health, reduce the risk of illness or injury, and improve overall well-being.

list.title: Focus:
list.snippet: On maintaining health and preventing illness, often through proactive measures.

list.title: Definition:
list.snippet: Treatment refers to the medical care provided to address an existing illness, injury, or condition.
Medications to manage chronic diseases like diabetes or high blood pressure.
Surgical procedures to repair injuries or remove diseased tissue.
Physical therapy to rehabilitate after an injury.

list.title: Goals:
list.snippet: To relieve symptoms, cure the illness or injury, and restore the patient's health and function.

list.title: Focus:
list.snippet: On addressing existing health issues and restoring health after illness or injury.

list.title: Timing:
list.snippet: Prevention happens before illness or injury, while treatment occurs after.

list.title: Focus:
list.snippet: Prevention focuses on maintaining health, while treatment focuses on restoring health.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: While both can have costs, prevention is often more cost-effective in the long run, as it can prevent or delay the need for more expensive treatments.

list.title: Effectiveness:
list.snippet: Prevention aims to be effective by reducing the risk of disease, while treatment aims to be effective by reducing the severity of a disease or injury.

text_blocks.snippet: In conclusion, both prevention and treatment are essential components of healthcare. A strong emphasis on prevention can reduce the burden of disease, while effective treatment is crucial for managing existing health problems.
